observation_summary: The Frequency.addValue(Object) method allowed non-Comparable objects to be added, which caused subsequent operations on the frequency table (a TreeMap) to fail with a ClassCastException. The API design was inconsistent, allowing the first non-comparable object but failing on subsequent additions.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the method signature to accept 'Comparable<?>' instead of 'Object' and delegating the original 'addValue(Object)' method to this new, more specific method. This is a correction to the method's parameter type and implementation logic to enforce the requirement that values must be comparable, which is a fundamental requirement for the underlying data structure (TreeMap). This fits the ODC definition of Algorithm/Method as it corrects the procedure/interface of the method to ensure correctness.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'the addValue(Object v) method allows one to add a plain Object, but one cannot add anything further to the instance, as the second add fails with IllegalArgumentException.'
The fix diff shows the addition of a new method 'public void addValue(Comparable<?>v)' and the modification of the existing 'addValue(Object v)' to call it.
The stack trace shows a ClassCastException occurring inside 'addValue' when interacting with the 'freqTable' (a TreeMap).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the method signature changed, the primary issue was the logic of allowing non-comparable objects into a structure that requires them, which is an algorithmic/correctness issue in the implementation of the frequency tracking.
The fix is not just adding a check, but changing the method signature to enforce the contract at the type level, which is a more fundamental change to the method's implementation.
